title: Empathetic advice-column register
description: This latent fires on the characteristic rhetorical moves of an advice-giver (e.g. Reddit relationship-advice or AITA style responses): validating the person's feelings, offering non-judgmental reassurance ('I'm not here to judge'), giving tentative interpretations of others' motives, suggesting a next step or perspective-taking action, and closing questions/prompts like 'What do you think?' or 'How does that sound?'. It activates on short empathetic hedges, reassurances, and advice-formula phrases ('It's important to remember...', 'That's a great starting point', 'You're not the asshole', 'Please know that...'), as well as speculative psychological explanations of a third party's behavior offered in a supportive counseling tone. It would not activate on neutral factual statements, narrative descriptions of events without evaluative/advisory framing, technical or unrelated instructional content lacking this empathetic-counselor voice, or purely declarative opinions stated without hedging or supportive framing.

title: Advice-column relationship discourse
description: This latent fires on sentences from the genre of interpersonal-advice text (e.g., Reddit relationship/AITA-style responses): validating statements, empathetic acknowledgments, short numbered or bolded advice-list items, reassurances ('it's okay', 'it's understandable'), suggestions of coping strategies, and clarifying follow-up questions posed to the person seeking advice. It activates on short declarative or interrogative sentences about emotions, boundaries, communication, and conflict resolution in personal relationships, as well as on the formatting artifacts (numbered/bulleted list markers, bold headers like '4. **') that structure such advice responses. It would not activate on neutral factual statements, technical or narrative content unrelated to interpersonal advice, or purely topic-specific detail lacking the advice/validation framing (e.g., a plain description of a dog breed or a URL) unless embedded within this reassurance-and-guidance structure.

title: Conversational advice-giving register
description: This latent fires on the stylistic register of AI-assistant-style advice/self-help writing: short, formulaic, second-person coaching sentences (list markers, bolded lead-in phrases like 'Listen actively:', 'Visualize success:', short reassurances 'Absolutely not.', empathetic validations 'You're not being spoiled...', rhetorical check-in questions 'Does that make sense?', suggested scripted dialogue in quotes, and transitional phrases like 'Now, here's where it gets tricky'). It activates on fragments that function as discrete steps, tips, reassurances, or conversational prompts within advice-giving or interpersonal-guidance text, including bare list numbers/bullets and bolded headers that structure such advice. It would not activate on purely factual, narrative, or technical content lacking this coaching/advice-giving conversational form, even if the topic (relationships, stress, planning) is similar, since the trigger is the register/structure rather than subject matter.

title: Transitional lead-in before a numbered list
description: This latent fires on short discourse-marker phrases that immediately precede an enumerated list of reasons, suggestions, or considerations, such as 'Here's why:', 'Here are some thoughts to consider:', or 'Here's a breakdown of the situation:'. It activates most strongly on the bare transitional stub itself (often followed directly by '1.' or '1. **'), functioning as a structural signpost that sets up upcoming itemized content rather than conveying substantive meaning. It also activates, more weakly, on related framing phrases like 'Here's where things get tricky' that signal a shift in the explanation without a list marker. It does not activate on the actual list items, general advice sentences, rhetorical questions (e.g., 'So, are you the asshole?'), or empathetic/evaluative statements that lack this list-introducing or transition-signaling function.

title: Recommending therapy or trusted support seeking
description: This latent fires on advice-giving sentences that explicitly recommend seeking out a therapist, counselor, or trusted friend/family member to talk through emotions, process feelings, or develop coping strategies. It activates most strongly on formulaic constructions like 'Consider talking to a therapist/trusted friend...' or 'They can help you work through your feelings/emotions and develop coping strategies,' where the sentence's core content is the referral itself rather than the emotional situation being described. It is weaker or absent on sentences that give other kinds of relational advice (e.g., use 'I' statements, set boundaries, have an honest conversation, practice self-care) even when they occur in similar advice-column contexts, since those lack the specific 'seek support/therapy/trusted person' recommendation pattern. It does not activate on general emotional narration, validation statements, or advice that doesn't involve directing the reader toward a third-party listener or professional.
